notes: Dragonfly's "brain": core avionics for commands and data, guidance and navigation, and communications in one box. Drawn from NASA/APL's full-resolution March 2026 photos: a black heat-sink top with fins parallel to the face and rows of fasteners, a copper ground strap, a silver face plate bolted round its edge with two rows of black connector windows, Micro-D connectors each mated to a labeled, silver-wrapped cable, and yellow tape strips. Mounted with its back to a wall panel beside a power switching unit, as photographed. No size is published: about 28 x 28 x 22 cm, scaled from the standard Micro-D connectors in the photos. The exact window layout (mostly hidden by cables in the photos), depth and which wall it is on are estimates. Temperature is the shared bay-air model. The first card column's upper and lower connector pairs now have estimated service bends, eight lacing ties and four face-mounted supports, guided by real NASA/APL hardware photographs and general NASA harness workmanship principles. The lower pair uses shorter, height-separated returns for its floor-level exits, with labels attached to its own wires and supports clear of connector bodies. All 26 lead endpoints, the enclosure and plug poses are unchanged; the other 22 cable paths still need installation review. Connector face, Upper cable pair and Lower cable pair are separate focus targets. Interfaces, Harnesses / lines and Mounts remain independently removable. Routing, support attachment, cable construction and actual circuit destinations are unverified; these bends are not flight-qualified, and geometric contact does not identify a flight splice or pinout. No new attic bus, hidden electronics or thermal/electrical solver is added.
